title: Strait of Hormuz: Two Ships Sink After Projectile Attacks
text:
Two ships sank in waters near the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday after projectile attacks. Iran is suspected of targeting civilian vessels, raising maritime security concerns.
Two ships sank in or near the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday after being hit by unidentified projectiles, according to maritime authorities. The attacks are widely presumed to have been carried out by Iran using missiles or drones. Iran claimed on Wednesday that one of the ships sank after hitting a mine laid in the strait by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps ( IRGC).
The vessel sustained damage and a fire on board while passing through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, and has since sunk, authorities said. The Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) expressed deep concern over the continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, calling them unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law.
Strait of Hormuz Shipping Attacks
The attacks mark the second and third ships sunk by Iranian terrorism since the conflict between the US and Iran began at the end of February. On September 23, another ship sank near the Strait of Hormuz after being left burning and adrift, resulting in one crew member killed.
On Thursday, EuroNews reported social media videos appearing to show cargo including mobile phones and luxury goods floating in the water near the strait, with people in small boats collecting items. The cargo is believed to have come from a sinking vessel.
Iranian state media claimed on Thursday that a cargo ship struck a naval mine while using an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz. The statement was accompanied by photos of a cargo ship sinking from its stern, dropping dozens of containers into the water, while smoke rose from its decks.
UKMTO Reports Projectile Damage
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) center said two unnamed container ships were struck by unknown projectiles while passing through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening. Both ships were able to continue after taking only minor damage.
Earlier, UKMTO reported that an oil tanker caught fire while passing through a prohibited zone in the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking systems turned off. The report claimed Iranian forces were monitoring the ship without taking credit for attacking it.
On March 4, another vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and abandoned. The details of that incident remain unclear.
Iran's New Tactics and Regional Impact
US officials told Reuters on Wednesday that Iran is using new tactics to attack civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to keep oil prices high to hurt President Donald Trump and his party in the midterm elections. The officials said the new tactics went into effect about ten days ago and have resulted in a surge of ships suffering damage as they attempt to transit the strait.
A US military official told Reuters one tactic appeared to involve using small spotter boats to target ships, instead of relying on radar installations that were largely destroyed by American airstrikes. US forces destroyed at least one of these spotter boats last week.
UKMTO and maritime tracking services said the Iranians also appear to be expanding their targeting area beyond the Strait of Hormuz, to include the waters of Oman and the UAE. Iranian officials predicted Iran's attacks would completely shut down the strait before the US elections in November.
One Iranian official said that just when they think they are getting close to the point where prices will fall, we will push them away from it. This is a game of chess. Such vessels would be safe nowhere, even outside the Strait of Hormuz.
